description: How the airline's customer roles relate to each other: corporate programs booking and funding traveller trips, operations control recovering travellers, families, and cargo when the network breaks, and the policy and performance loops that close the journey.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Booking and contracting of managed travel and cargo capacity

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Day-of-operations recovery, ground coordination, and shipment handling

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Central billing and settlement of travel spend

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Policy, disruption updates, and experience feedback

relations.name: Books managed long-haul travel
relations.description: Books policy-compliant long-haul trips for frequent-flying employees against negotiated corporate fares and preferred cabin rules.

relations.name: Funds trips through central billing
relations.description: Pays employee trips through lodge cards and central billing, then reconciles fares, extras, and changes against the travel program budget.

relations.name: Sets travel policy and duty of care
relations.description: Communicates cabin and routing policy, approval rules, and duty-of-care expectations so travellers know what is bookable and who acts for them in a disruption.

relations.name: Feeds back trip experience and compliance
relations.description: Returns trip satisfaction, disruption impact, and out-of-policy booking signals that the program manager uses in supplier reviews and policy tuning.

relations.name: Recovers disrupted premium journeys
relations.description: Rebooks high-value travellers during irregular operations, protecting connections and status entitlements before the traveller has to queue or call.

relations.name: Keeps family holidays intact through disruption
relations.description: Reaccommodates whole family bookings together and coordinates the ground journey so a delayed leg does not unravel the holiday they saved for.

relations.name: Raises family assistance needs
relations.description: Registers special assistance, seating-together, and infant needs that ground coordination must honor at every airport touchpoint of the trip.

relations.name: Responds with rebooking preferences
relations.description: Accepts or adjusts proposed recovery options through self-service, giving operations control fast signal on which reaccommodation solutions actually land.

relations.name: Tenders shipments for belly uplift
relations.description: Delivers time-sensitive and high-value shipments for uplift on booked long-haul capacity and works exceptions with operations when a shipment risks missing its milestone.

relations.name: Notifies capacity changes and cargo milestones
relations.description: Alerts forwarders when aircraft swaps or disruptions cut belly capacity and pushes milestone status so they can re-plan valuable shipments early.
